articles.title: Always tired? Leaving your ‘loops’ open may be the unexpected cause
articles.summary: Procrastinating on some tasks may feel harmless, but the perpetual mental hum of unfinished business may cause more stress than you realize.
articles.body:
The texts you've ignored, the vacation supplies you still need to order, the hard conversation you've been avoiding — repeatedly putting off such tasks because they feel too daunting may seem relatively harmless. But the constant mental hum of unfinished business may be more draining than you realize — like your laptop slowing and glitching because you have 90 browser tabs open.

Some people are waking up to that reality, sharing on social media and in podcasts their epiphanies about the countless open "loops" in their lives in need of closing. The buzzy phrase helps them more easily recognize and combat the habit.

As New Yorker Florence Friebe learned about open loops, she began to see the pattern in her own life — for example, via a hole in her jacket pocket that she kept neglecting to fix and remembered every time she dropped her keys or phone into it.

"I could really start seeing how many repetitive thoughts I was carrying, and how much space it was taking," added Friebe, cohost of the podcast "2 Curly Haired Girls With ADHD" — referring not only to the effects of procrastinating on fixing her jacket pocket but also on cleaning and work tasks.

Psychologists who study procrastination say these people are right to address these issues.

The inertia comes from perceiving "the 'cost' of doing the task in terms of time, energy, and emotional fatigue," said Dr. Vara Saripalli, a clinical psychologist in private practice in Chicago, via email. "They aren't thinking about the other negatives that ensue from waiting; they're focused on the present and avoiding unpleasantness in the here and now."

But as Friebe learned, avoidance also can be highly costly, both practically and by taking up energy that could be used for other things, Saripalli added.

Procrastination and chronic stress can eventually take a toll on both your mental and physical health, said Dr. Fuschia Sirois, professor of social and health psychology at Durham University in England. Sirois, a procrastination expert who has been studying the issue for 25 years, is also the author of "Procrastination: What It Is, Why It's a Problem, and What You Can Do About It."

Those impacts include causing or contributing to a weakened immune system, chronic disease, anxiety and digestive issues, low self-esteem and loneliness, Sirois added.

For Lanna, a content creator and Pilates instructor in Germany, procrastination-related worries even caused stomachaches, she said. Lanna requested that CNN use her nickname for privacy.

But for many people, awareness of these impacts doesn't always make taking action easier.

For generally healthy people, habitual procrastination typically boils down to two causes, even if the details differ per individual, experts said: negative emotions associated with certain tasks or with the prospect of those tasks not going well.

Maybe you're delaying replying to a text because you haven't figured out a perfect response, and you have complicated feelings around imperfection. Or maybe you're avoiding a serious talk with a friend because you're people-pleasing or worried you'll be hurt. (You can read more about procrastination "styles" and related tips here .)

Procrastinating on relatively minor things sometimes may stem from a broader societal shift Saripalli has noticed, in which people are less comfortable with finality and losing options, she said. "The simple task of returning a package becomes an internal monologue of, 'What if I change my mind and I can't get this item again? I'm better off holding on to it till I'm sure.'"

On the other hand, you may just have too many responsibilities and need to consider which ones you can forgo. Maybe you're exhausted by other commitments or spending too much time on your phone, which can be a distraction and energy zapper.

Or maybe the cause of your procrastination is more complicated. If you're struggling to overcome procrastination on your own, consider seeing a doctor or therapist to determine whether there's a more serious underlying issue, Sirois said — such as depression, ADHD or an anxiety disorder.

These disorders can make one's tolerance of negative feelings about a task much lower, Sirois added. That, as well as other symptoms, can contribute to people with these disorders being more prone to procrastinate.

In those cases, some coping strategies can help, but they don't cure disorders or replace professional assistance, Sirois said.

That was true for Lanna, who said she has ADHD and autism, and for Friebe. Friebe said she realized that her struggles with procrastination were significantly tied to her ADHD, depression and polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome , or PMOS.

"It was almost like I was lacking ingredients," Friebe said. "Once I got diagnosed, it felt like a giant relief."

Awareness of your urges to procrastinate and of the likely consequences can sometimes be enough to help you regulate your emotions, then choose differently.

But some people such as Friebe and Lanna have also sought professional help for their conditions and improved their lifestyle habits. These changes have given them more energy and the confidence to be more efficient.

Seeing a therapist can really be helpful for anyone regardless of whether you have a condition since they can help you deal with pessimistic ideas causing procrastination. Sirois recently released a free, online evidence-based tool kit for that purpose.

Now Friebe schedules free time to tackle whatever tasks she's got at the moment. Doing a job little by little — or styling to-do list tasks that way — has been more effective than anticipating it with the all-or-nothing thinking that can make responsibilities feel daunting. What also helps Lanna is doing activities that rejuvenate her.

And Friebe really means little , even if that feels stupid, she said. She referred to a story she heard of people who wanted to start exercising at a gym driving to the gym, as they were, on the days they had said they wanted to work out — but not going inside.

The next time, those people also put on workout clothes before driving. Next, they went to the gym in their outfits and exercised for only five minutes. "What they were actually building was trust that they were reliable, that they could do it, so then it could accumulate," Friebe said. "Before you knew it, they were working out."

Studies support the effectiveness of such gradual habit-building.

Guilt and shame are the two most common emotions people feel when they procrastinate, Sirois said, which compound the problem and further paralyze you — even though taking action would alleviate all those negative feelings. "Being self-compassionate is actually a more effective way to get oneself back on track," she added.

Acknowledge that you're struggling and what you're feeling, and ask yourself whether the situation at hand will really be that bad. "Often, we anticipate things are going to be much worse than what they are," Sirois said. Even if your attempts don't go well, trust that you can learn how to navigate the fallout and be OK.

Also try to find the meaning in different responsibilities, those interviewed recommended. If you're delaying cleaning your room and beating yourself up about whether your roommate is judging you for the mess, think about the fact that you deserve a clean, cozy space.

Friebe and Lanna consider how productivity might bring them closer to their life purpose or the person they want to be. And if a heart-to-heart goes poorly, even then, the meaning can be that you grew in your ability to handle conflict, and that you have the truth about the relationship and can act accordingly.

If you're avoiding scheduling a doctor's appointment because you don't want to hear their feedback, your health issue exists regardless. So why not get some answers and prevent your problem from worsening? Regardless of the task, think of how relaxed you'll feel and how much time you'll free up for other fun things if you just get it done.

Since Friebe has improved her health and learned what strategies work for her, "the way I speak to myself is completely different," she said.

"I have a better sense of self and identity and self-trust," Friebe added. "My entire life has changed. I'm a different person."

articles.title: What should you wear through airport security? Frequent fliers recommend these fuss-free pieces
articles.summary: Consider this your cheat sheet for a smoother trip through TSA lines — not to mention a smoother trip overall.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

Getting through airport security is stressful enough, so your outfit shouldn't be the thing holding up the line. Looking polished is always a plus, but the best travel outfits work smarter, not harder. Think easy-on, easy-off shoes , layers that don't require a full wardrobe change and clever pieces that keep you from frantically digging through your bag while everyone behind you silently judges.

So, what actually deserves a spot in your airport uniform? We asked frequent fliers to share their wardrobe standbys. From shoes made for breezing through security to fuss-free layers and smart, travel-friendly details, consider this your boarding pass for getting through the airport with less hassle — and more time for the important things, like finding your gate and grabbing a snack (or maybe a pre-flight glass of wine).

These things don't have to be on opposite sides of the terminal. The best travel outfits hit that sweet spot: Soft, stretchy and roomy enough to survive hours in a cramped seat, but polished enough that you won't be rushing to change the second you land. "I think comfort and style go hand in hand," says travel YouTuber Ally Gibson . "Comfort is non-negotiable, especially on long-haul flights. That said, you never know who you might meet, and looking good makes you feel good throughout the day."

Sometimes the secret to a comfortable travel outfit is less what you wear and more what you leave at home. "I avoid jeans, belts and anything tight because sitting in restrictive clothing becomes uncomfortable on a long travel day, especially when your body can feel more swollen during a flight," explains travel blogger Hazel McKinlay .

And while the days of dressing formally for a flight may be long gone, that doesn't mean airport style has to look like pajamas. "Comfort is definitely No. 1 for me, but I still want to look nice!" says Megan Miele, account manager of business travel at Cadence Travel . "My mom was a flight attendant and started flying back in 1969. Back then, you dressed up to the nines to get on an airplane. Flying was more of a privilege and was much more exclusive than it is today.

"Now, almost everyone can afford to fly, and we fly a LOT more often. We also have so many more rules and regulations to deal with. So for me, comfort is definitely the priority, but I still want to feel like I look put together. I'm not trying to show up at the airport looking like I just rolled out of bed," she added.

The modern-day happy medium? Start with pieces you can comfortably sit, stand and sprint to your gate in, then lean on a few smart styling tricks to make your travel look more polished. Layer a chic, cozy sweater over a soft T-shirt and leggings for an easy upgrade, or take the guesswork out of getting dressed with a cute matching set .

Colorfulkoala High-Waisted Tummy-Control Leggings

The best airport outfits include pieces that work smarter, not harder, especially when you're juggling a suitcase, a boarding pass and an overpriced airport coffee. "Layers are useful because airport and aircraft temperatures can vary so much. In colder weather I always take a scarf, which earns its place in my hand luggage several times over: I wear it at the airport and then use it as a blanket, wrap or makeshift pillow on the plane," says McKinlay.

Andrés Serra, trip planner and head of operations at Optimise Travel , has his travel-day formula down to a science. "My favorite travel outfit is a plain T-shirt, elastic-waist travel pants with two zipped pockets, a thin button-up overshirt and low-profile sneakers. The overshirt acts as a light jacket and can be rolled up to support my neck if I need it, and the pants are comfortable for long flights but still look good enough for a restaurant after landing." Cara Laban, founder of TravelReddi , agrees that pockets are a travel-day must. "I recommend pants with large pockets so you can easily grab essentials like your ID or passport and phone without having to dig through your bag," she says.

Choosing travel pieces that pull double duty doesn't just make the journey more comfortable — it also frees up precious space in your suitcase . A button-up can double as a pillow, an oversized scarf becomes an in-flight blanket and a pair of polished pants can hold your essentials and take you straight from a cramped coach seat to dinner without an outfit change. The more versatile each piece is, the less you have to pack.

And don't forget about what's underneath your outfit. Gibson recommends compression socks for long travel days, calling them "a game-changer for leg fatigue and circulation." They may not be the star of your airport look, but your legs could be thanking you by the time you land.

What items help you breeze through airport security?

A little pre-security prep can mean the difference between an easy trip through the checkpoint and becoming that person frantically scooping up loose change and jewelry while the line piles up behind you. "The most useful thing I bring isn't something I wear," says Serra. "It's a small zipped pouch I keep in my personal bag. Before I leave for the airport, I put my watch, coins, wallet, earbuds and other small items inside. TSA suggests putting pocket items in your carry-on instead of leaving valuables loose in a screening tray. This also saves me from scrambling to grab everything while other people are waiting."

Your bag can also do some of the heavy lifting. "If you are traveling with a laptop or iPad, a bag with a separate laptop compartment will make it much easier to get it in and out at security," explains Laban. She also recommends skipping jewelry and belts loaded with metal, since they can add another thing to remove — and another thing to remember on the other side.

And don't forget the right shoes. "If you don't have TSA PreCheck (which I highly recommend), then slip-on shoes, or just shoes that don't have difficult laces, are definitely helpful," Laban adds.

Gibson swears by a crossbody with plenty of pockets, like her go-to Bandolier bag . "It keeps my phone, ID, passport, wallet, headphones and lip gloss within reach. There's even a dedicated front phone pocket, which makes keeping track of everything at security a breeze." Everything should have a designated spot, so you can spend less time digging through your bag at security and more time relaxing in the airport lounge.

articles.title: UnitedHealth Stock's Biggest Risk Sits In The Commercial Book
articles.summary: Medicare's improvement is real but not a turn in cost trend, while commercial costs keep running higher and the margin fix there has slipped again.
articles.body:
Medicare's improvement is real but not a turn in cost trend, while commercial costs keep running higher and the margin fix there has slipped again.

UnitedHealth (UNH) shares are up about 34% over the past year, ahead of the S&P 500's 21%, on a recovery in margins the company is only partway through. Two of the moving parts in that recovery are pulling in opposite directions, and the one that is deteriorating has no date on its fix.

Year-over-year revenue growth, after topping 12% for two straight quarters, has stepped down over the last two periods to 2.0% and now 0.4%, and the company has intentionally prioritized margin discipline over top-line volume. UnitedHealthcare expects full-year 2026 Medicare Advantage enrollment to decline by approximately 1.1 million through benefit adjustments and selective changes in market participation aimed at margin stability. On $450.1 billion of trailing-twelve-month revenue, that is a business trading size for profitability, and with the top line flat every dollar of earnings recovery now has to come out of cost.

Medicare Is Improving Without The Trend Inflecting

Medicare is where the repair is working . Management expects the 2026 Medicare medical cost trend to come in below its initial estimate of around 10%, pointing first to its own benefit design, care management models and network curation. Management also names a more favorable respiratory season and weather patterns alongside them. The company-wide reported second-quarter medical care ratio of 86.7% was itself helped by $860 million of net favorable prior period medical development, the majority of which was in-year development. Management is explicit that the softer Medicare trend is not an inflection point.

An Ineffective Arbitration Process Is Adding Cost

The commercial side is going the other way. Commercial medical cost trend is running modestly above the 11% the company had been seeing. The independent resolution process under the No Surprises Act, which applies only to commercial plans, is adding 50 basis points or so of incremental trend in 2026 and now totals at least 100 basis points of cost. The company's management characterizes the process as inefficient, noting that dispute filings are heavily concentrated among a small number of provider groups. Add provider coding intensity in office visits and emergency departments, and full commercial margin recovery has been pushed past 2027 . Margin repair on a timetable that keeps moving is a different proposition from the strong margins the Trefis High Quality Portfolio looks for in its holdings.

articles.summary: If you have bad credit, you need to find ways to compensate for the additional risk.
articles.body:
A credit score of at least 620 will qualify you for a conventional refinance — but clearing the minimum doesn't guarantee a good rate. Lenders save their best pricing for borrowers well above the cutoff, and the difference can add up to real money over the life of the loan.

Minimums vary by loan type: 580 for FHA, generally 700+ for jumbo, and no set agency floor for VA or USDA (though lenders typically look for 620 and 640 respectively). A score that rules out one option may still work for another.

If your score is borderline, run the math on closing costs vs. savings before you refinance — sometimes it's cheaper to spend a few months improving your score first.

If your score is well below your loan type's minimum, refinancing may not be your best move right now. A repayment plan or loan modification through your current servicer can offer payment relief without locking you into a new rate for years.

Meeting the minimum credit score for your loan type is only step one. Lenders price loans on a sliding scale, so qualifying and getting the best available rate are two different things — and the gap between a borderline score and a strong one can cost you real money over the life of the loan. Some low-score borrowers can benefit from government-backed streamline refinances, which forgo the credit check altogether.

Keep in mind that if your new rate isn't a real improvement over your current one, refinancing may actually cost you more than it saves once you factor in closing costs. Taking the time to improve your credit score can unlock access to a lower rate when you apply.

Read on for the minimum score you'll need by loan type and how to decide whether refinancing with bad credit — or not refinancing at all — is the right call.

What credit score is needed to refinance a house?

No credit minimum from VA, but lenders generally require 620

No credit minimum from USDA, but lenders generally require 640

These numbers are guidelines. The credit score you need to refinance depends on your lender, your individual situation and the type of refinance you choose. For example, lenders tend to have more stringent requirements for a cash-out refi than a traditional rate-and-term refinance.

You might also find that your lender wants a higher score if other parts of your financial picture aren't as strong, for instance, if you have a high debt-to-income (DTI) ratio .

articles.title: 9 commons myths about wrinkles debunked — and what dermatologists want you to know instead
articles.summary: From the importance of genetics to whether $200 moisturizers are a good buy, here's the whole truth and nothing but the truth.
articles.body:

I once read about a lady who didn't smile for over 40 years . Her reason for such a stationary expression was not a distaste for joy and laughter, but something else entirely — to prevent wrinkles . She'd decided that maintaining a straight, expressionless face was worth it to keep smooth, youthful-looking skin. (Apparently, she even resisted smiling when her daughter was born! Can you imagine?)

Sometimes, when I'm slathering on my lotions and potions in the evening, I think about this woman. Not because it's a cautionary tale about vanity, but because her fear wasn't necessarily directed at the right thing. Wrinkle mythology is full of misplaced fears and misplaced faith. We treat certain habits like miracle workers and others like poison, often with evidence pointed in the opposite direction. So, instead of guessing what to do and what to avoid, I asked dermatologists to bust some wrinkle myths and misconceptions. (But as the great Oscar Wilde once said, "The truth is rarely pure and never simple.")

Myth #1: Facial expressions are the main cause of wrinkles

Let's address the aforementioned smile-averse situation. If we stop facial movement, whether it's a smile, frown or Elvis-like lip snarl, it would stop wrinkles, right? According to Dr. Behrooz Torkian , a double board-certified facial plastic surgeon based in Beverly Hills, Calif., it's not that simple. Now, some wrinkles really are caused by movement: "A prime example of this is the wrinkles on the forehead, the glabella, or so-called 'elevens,' and the crow's feet," he says. But movement is also competing with bigger forces like sun exposure and collagen loss. His advice is to limit repetitive movement with Botox where it matters, and protect collagen with adequate SPF , a good diet, stress control and no smoking.

To rebuild collagen, Torkian recommends vitamin C , retinoids , growth factors and peptides , along with regular microneedling, radio frequency and laser treatments. And if you happen to have a red light mask in your closet, now's the time to break it out. "Recent scientific evidence on red light therapy has also supported the use of red and near-infrared light to support the metabolic processes of building collagen in the skin," he says.

Myth #2: How much you wrinkle depends solely on genetics

Your bloodline may set things up for your skin, but it doesn't decide the outcome alone. "Genetics matter because your genes shape how thick your skin is, how well you hold onto collagen and how much melanin you have doing built-in sun protection," says Dr. Geeta Yadav, a board-certified dermatologist and founder of Facet Dermatology. This is part of why some people "start creasing in their 30s while others sail into their 60s looking smooth."

However, she points out how identical twins with identical DNA can look years apart in age. She underscores the sun's impact on our skin, which makes movement seem like a minor threat by comparison. "Sun alone is estimated to account for around 80% of the visible aging we see on the face," she says.

Myth #3: The more expensive the moisturizer, the better

By now, you probably know that drugstore beauty can go toe-to-toe with luxury brands , and moisture is no exception. "I have always believed that paying a lot for a moisturizer is not worth it," says Torkian. What matters, he says, is what's actually in the jar. Moisturizers break down into three parts: humectants that draw in water, emollients that soften and occlusives that seal it all in. Beyond that, you want to consider whether it has actives, such as peptides, retinoids, hydroxy acids and niacinamide. "As a general rule, I personally avoid the super expensive and the super cheap," he says.

Myth #4: Dry skin causes wrinkles; oily skin ages better

"One of the most essential factors in the appearance of wrinkles in skin is the hydration of the collagen, hyaluronic acid and elastin within the dermis and epidermis," explains Torkian. Oil definitely supports it, as more sebaceous glands mean the skin has a built-in defense system against losing that moisture. However, dry skin doesn't necessarily mean you're doomed. It just needs that same protection in a different way: "Moisturizers such as ceramides to augment the skin barrier" versus retinoids and hydroxy acids for oily skin — at least as a starting point.

According to Torkian, internal hydration is definitely a part of the picture, but only if the skin barrier is already intact and topical moisture is in place. But water alone doesn't do the plumping. A 2015 study published in Clinical, Cosmetic and Investigational Dermatology showed that adding roughly 2 liters of water a day to women's diets for a month significantly improved skin hydration and biomechanics.

Ultimately, it's less that water plumps wrinkles and more that dehydration accelerates them. Yadav is more blunt, saying that drinking more water is unlikely to meaningfully change wrinkles.

Myth #6: Retinol and tretinoin are interchangeable

Both retinol and tretinoin speed up cell turnover and rebuild collagen, which smooths and softens wrinkles over time. But the real question is which one gets you there and how fast. Torkian breaks down how tretinoin is the active compound itself, whereas retinol has to go through two steps to convert into tretinoin. "This means that using tretinoin can lead to quicker results and quicker onset of the results, but it can also feel a little bit more harsh to skin that has not adjusted to retinoic acid yet," he says. Over the long term, results from both can be very similar, he adds.

Myth #7: Only in-office procedures can reverse wrinkles, not topicals

According to Torkian, the answer to this isn't a flat no. "There are some topicals that can be very helpful in reversing wrinkling," he says, "provided that the wrinkling has not gone out of hand." Retinoids, especially prescription tretinoin, have decades of trial evidence behind them, while vitamin C, growth factors and peptides can also make a difference.

But he doesn't stop there: "Another essential factor is whether proper prevention is being employed at the same time as using the topical that is intended to reverse wrinkling." In other words, a product working solo, without sun protection or consistency, applied to wrinkles that are already deeply set isn't a fair test of what topicals can actually do.

Myth #8: The neck and chest age faster than the face

While it's true that the skin on the neck and chest is very different from the skin on the face (mainly because there are fewer oil glands), Torkian pushes back on the framing of this myth, and points out the impact of our behavior. "One thing to keep in mind about the skin of the neck and chest is that they rarely get any love," he says. "I always like to remind my patients that when they have their skin-care routine, they should not forget the neck and chest. It is natural to want to use all of your expensive skin-care products on what you feel people are looking at the most, but spreading a little love below the chin can be impactful over time in preventing neck and chest aging."

Myth #9: Botox is the best treatment for all kinds of wrinkles

Yadav is clear that Botox is excellent for softening the dynamic lines caused by repeated muscle movement. "Frown lines, forehead lines and crow's feet respond beautifully, because quieting the muscle stops it folding the skin above it thousands of times a day," she explains. But it does much less for lines already etched in when your face is completely at rest, and very little for crepey texture, sun damage or the sagging that comes from lost volume and laxity, she says.

At under $10, this effective cream is proof of Myth #3 — you don't have to splurge to get real results. It pairs retinol with bakuchiol, a plant-derived retinol alternative that helps soften irritation, plus vitamin E and allantoin to keep skin calm. You get softer-looking lines and plumper, less flakey skin without the retinol redness.

One of the most effective anti-aging treatments available without a prescription is Differin. This dermatologist favorite can help improve skin texture, fine lines and overall skin tone as long as you're consistent. It can also help build collagen, which, in turn, makes skin look brighter and bouncier.

This budget-friendly moisturizer does barrier-repair work while you sleep thanks to a powerful trio of ceramides, hyaluronic acid and peptides. It's essentially the ingredient-category cheat sheet from Myth #6 packed into an affordable cream.

Vichy Mineral 89 Booster, Hyaluronic Acid Serum

We voted this the best drugstore face serum for a reason. It contains Vichy's legendary Volcanic Water, which is sourced from French volcanoes and contains 15 essential minerals that strengthen, protect and repair the skin barrier​.

Celimax The Vita-A Retinal Shot Tightening Dual Cream

This Celimax cream features a two-in-one dispenser, releasing a retinal cream with 5% panthenol soothing cream at the same time. It also explicitly treats the neck alongside the face with matrixyl 3000, a peptide complex, for firming, so you can make sure Myth #8 gets covered.

articles.title: United's biggest-ever international expansion includes 10 destinations worth a closer look
articles.summary: The Chicago-based carrier will offer new nonstop flights across Europe and Asia, making places like Marseille, Valencia and Okinawa easier to reach.
articles.body:
Ever wanted to fly nonstop to Slovenia? You're in Luxembourg!

United Airlines on Tuesday announced what the airline says is the largest expansion in its history, with 10 new international destinations — including the first nonstop flights by a U.S. airline to Ljubljana, Slovenia and Luxembourg City — and 13 new routes.

"We've opened up more of the world to our customers," Patrick Quayle, United's senior vice president of global network planning, said on a conference call with reporters . "Next summer, we'll give them more opportunities … to explore places that they may not have previously considered."

Beginning in March 2027 and continuing into the summer, United will launch nonstop service to the following destinations across Europe and Asia:

Luxembourg City, Luxembourg — from Newark

Terceira, Azores, Portugal — from Newark

Toulouse, France — from Washington Dulles

The flights to Ibiza, Valencia, Luxembourg City, Marseille and Toulouse will be aboard United's new Airbus A321XLR. The plane is scheduled to begin flying select domestic routes in September, followed by international service in December.

The Chicago-based carrier has added nearly 60 international destinations to its route map since 2017, and now flies to more than 160 international destinations.

United is also adding new international routes to destinations it already serves from three of its U.S. hubs: daily service from Los Angeles to Osaka, Japan; nonstop service from Washington, D.C., to Milan, Italy; and daily nonstop service from Denver to Paris.

The airline said it will also resume three-times-weekly service from San Francisco to Tel Aviv on March 28, 2027.

articles.title: Unitree post-IPO slide ignites bubble concerns
articles.summary: The Chinese robot maker’s shares have retreated more than 45% from their debut peak.
articles.body:
Shares in Chinese robot maker Unitree have retreated more than 45% from their debut peak, inflicting pain on retail investors and prompting bubble fears.

"Investors were carried ​away by the technology revolution narrative ," a Beijing asset manager told Reuters.

China's newest corporate star , Unitree's founder has downplayed expectations, saying the firm is " lagging behind " in real-world applications.

A flood of new tech shares hitting the market in Hong Kong and Shanghai has worried investors: Alibaba's record share sale, coupled with the massive IPO plans of memory chipmaker YMTC, caused the industry writ large to take a hit on concerns that more Chinese tech firms will follow, "essentially spreading the cost of AI investment across the public and investors ," one analyst said.

articles.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement of a blockbuster case accusing the company of deliberately des...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Meta Platforms Inc. and state attorneys general have discussed a possible mid-trial settlement of a blockbuster case accusing the company of deliberately designing Facebook and Instagram to addict teens, people familiar with the matter said.

Lutnick's Intervention in Canada Talks Draws Praise, Blame

Apple Gears Up to Launch Its First New Mac Mini in Two Years

Bessent's Mentor Druckenmiller Calls Bond Buying a Mistake

Carney Matches Trump Tariffs With 50% Tax on US Dairy, Steel

Xi Signals Defiance as US Threatens Sanctions Over Iran Help

The trial, now in its second week in federal court in Oakland, California, poses an enormous risk for Meta as the top legal officers of 29 states are seeking both massive financial penalties on behalf of the public and mandatory changes to how the platforms operate. The people familiar with settlement talks asked not to be identified due to their sensitivity.

A spokesperson for Meta had no immediate comment. A representative of the attorney general's office in California declined to comment. Representatives of the other three states leading the case, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey, didn't immediately respond to requests for comment.

The states have alleged violations of state consumer protection and federal privacy laws — which carry fines that add up quickly when multiplied by millions of young Instagram and Facebook users.

Meta has denied the states' allegations and accused the attorneys general of seeking unreasonable design changes and an "outlandish payout."

By Meta's own calculations, a loss at trial could saddle it with penalties of as much as $1.4 trillion, an amount close to its market capitalization and unheard of in the annals of legal history. A settlement would likely amount to a far smaller sum.

During the first week of testimony at the trial, jurors heard from Instagram head Adam Mosseri and a collection of current and former Meta employees who helped design its social media platforms and study how teen users interact with tools designed to cut down on problematic use.

Lawyers have said they also expect to call Meta founder and chief executive officer Mark Zuckerberg to testify.

The four attorneys general spearheading the case alleged under their separate state laws that Meta knowingly designed features that encouraged compulsive and prolonged use of its platforms by young people, while simultaneously misleading consumers about safety features.

The broader bipartisan group of 29 states accused the company of collecting data from users under 13 years old in violation of the federal Children's Online Privacy Protection Act.

articles.title: College student fatally shot by police after knocking on wrong door
articles.summary: Glenn Pysher was trying to find his friends when he accidentally knocked on the door of the wrong house. The homeowners called 911 to report an attempted bre...
articles.body:
A 22-year-old college student was fatally shot by police over the weekend after he accidentally knocked on the wrong door of a home in Pennsylvania, and now his parents are demanding answers.

Glenn Pysher, known to his family and friends as Bubba, spent Saturday night celebrating with friends at a local bar in Upper Pottsgrove, Pennsylvania. When the group decided to move the party to a house nearby, Pysher walked there alone and mistakenly knocked on the wrong door.

His mother, Erin Pysher, said she thinks he got "mixed up" because the house is in a wooded area.

The homeowners called 911 to report an attempted break-in. Police arrived early Sunday and found Pysher in the back of the home.

"So he probably was knocking, 'Hey, let me in, where are you at, what are you doing?' And the homeowners thought he was trying to break into the house and called the cops," his mother told CBS News about what she thinks happened.

There, the Montgomery County District Attorney's Office said, an encounter ensued, and Glenn Pysher was shot and killed. The Upper Pottsgrove Police Department has not released any information about the shooting, but said the incident was under investigation.

"At 12:32, we have the call log, he was talking on the phone with his friends," his mother told CBS News. "By 12:35, I believe, the cops had already shown up and shot him."

"No Taser. No nothing. Automatic deadly force," she said, adding that the family hasn't heard anything from the police department. The Montgomery County Detective Bureau did not respond to CBS News' request for comment.

"I just want things to be done right. I want to know the facts," his father, Glenwood Pysher, said.

Erin Pysher says her son loved playing baseball, and he was looking forward to playing at Saint Elizabeth University in Florham Park, New Jersey, where he recently transferred.

"I was going to take him to school and help him set up his dorm room. He was supposed to start classes on Monday," his mother said. "It's unreal. I don't even know how to explain it. It's a feeling of so much sadness in my heart. I can't — it's hard to breathe."

"He was such a good kid," Glenwood Pysher told CBS News. "The community here loved him, and nobody can believe this happened to this young man who wouldn't hurt a fly."

articles.title: Dozens killed in rebel attacks on Sudan’s Kordofan, medical group says
articles.summary: Sudan Doctors Network says SPLM-N rebels killed 27 people in South Kordofan, including four children.
articles.body:
A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kordofan.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sudan Doctors Network said the killings were carried out by the Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas inhabited by the Otoro tribe in South Kordofan.

"The attacks resulted in a large wave of displacement among citizens towards the Abu Hitan area and Kadugli," it said.

Targeting unarmed civilians on ethnic grounds constitutes a "clear violation of international humanitarian law", the group added, warning that continued violations threatened to turn "the conflict in South Kordofan into a broader ethnic conflict".

The killings follow intense fighting earlier this year between forces linked to SPLM-N and the Otoro tribe, which is a minority group in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan.

The ethnic standoff, first instigated by land disputes, adds another layer to the country's ongoing civil war , which broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese army and the RSF.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country's population, require humanitarian assistance.

articles.title: Chinese artist Gao Zhen sentenced to 3 years in prison over satirical Mao artworks
articles.summary: Gao Zhen, who is based in the U.S., was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024 and charged over works that authorities deemed insulting to revolutionary figures.
articles.body: BANGKOK — Chinese artist Gao Zhen was sentenced to three years in prison Tuesday for “infringing upon the reputation of heroes” through his satirical works of art, including statues of China’s former leader Mao Zedong. The U.S.-based Gao, who was part of an artistic duo known internationally as the Gao Brothers, was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024. He has been in official custody since then. He was sentenced by the Sanhei People’s Court in northern Hebei province, according to his wife, Zhao Yaliang. The charges against Gao relate to artistic works that China’s authorities deem insulting to revolutionary figures. One was a 2009 statue called “Mao’s Guilt,” which shows the former leader and founder of modern China kneeling in repentance, and another was the “Miss Mao” series of caricatures depicting Mao with breasts and an engorged nose. Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders, who has been advocating for Gao’s case, described the sentence as “a very clear case of a violation of a person’s freedom of expression.” Yi said the artist plans to appeal the sentence and noted that the artworks in question were created before the law Gao was sentenced with had been passed. The court did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Amnesty International criticized the court sentence, which it described as a deterrent against artistic expression. “The lengthy pretrial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offense illustrate the authorities’ determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression,” said Amnesty’s China director, Sarah Brooks. “No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history,” she said. Zhao said she hopes to be reunited with her husband and be able to return to the U.S., where the family had immigrated. “I felt two years was my limit, and I was really disappointed and sad. I haven’t been able to catch my breath,” she said. She had prepared clothes for her husband hoping that he would be released. Chinese courts often count pretrial detention as time served in a sentence. The Gao Brothers, whose works addressed themes of authoritarianism and censorship, became famous in a time of relative openness in China and were exhibited both inside the country and abroad. However, in recent years, the state has increased its controlling grip on certain aspects of expression, especially in regard to political figures with the passage of the law in 2018 that bans criticism of the nation’s heroes.

articles.title: Chinese humanoid robot that beat Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint record does it again, but even faster
articles.summary: The race was part of the World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition in Beijing that showcases China’s rapid advances in robotics amid growing rivalry with the U.S.
articles.body: BEIJING — A Chinese humanoid robot set a new 100-meter sprint record of 8.86 seconds in Beijing on Tuesday, beating its robot competitors — and the fastest recorded human time. The race was part of China’s World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition now in its second year in Beijing. The event is also a showcase for China’s rapid advances in robotics amid an intensifying technology rivalry with the U.S. The Tiangong Ultra humanoid robot beat its own record of 9.39 seconds it had set just three days earlier at the event’s opening on Saturday. For comparison, the men’s 100-meter world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt in 2009. Experts are amazed to see such progress in the humanoid robot industry. “This is a significant milestone — not simply because the robot ran faster than a human, but because of what it takes to make a bipedal robot run at this speed,” said Dennis Hong, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles. “As speed increases, balance, control, impacts, actuator performance and mechanical robustness all become much more challenging,” Hong said. The record-breaking robot fell after hitting the finish line, a padded barrier, with sparks flying from its waist. Hong pointed out that the fall leads to more meaningful and difficult questions: whether robots can move and stop safely, recognize unexpected obstacles, recover from mistakes and continue working, the capabilities that ultimately make them more useful. The games feature over 1,300 competitions involving more than 2,000 robots in 51 events like running, long jump and table tennis, as well as ballroom dancing. Unlike the traditional Olympics, the robots also compete in teams in real-world scenarios, including household tasks, hotel services and emergency response. “’Housekeeper’ and ‘caregiver’ robots are still in the pilot and validation phase,” China’s official newspaper People’s Daily said Monday, but “challenges are precisely where the focus of development lies. … China’s robotics industry is evolving toward higher quality and innovation.”

articles.title: Video from Colombia quake falsely linked to Peru tremor
articles.summary: After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows v...
articles.body:
After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows visuals from the tremor. The footage was in fact filmed in the Colombian city of Pereira after a 7.4-magnitude quake struck the country a week prior.

"Peru is in chaos. A powerful 7.2-magnitude earthquake has just struck the Ayacucho region in the south of the country," says a Chinese-language Douyin post shared on August 21, 2026.

The video shows the upper half of a blue building collapsing and debris falling as a man yells, "grandma, grandma...no...no" in Spanish.

A strong 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck southern Peru on August 20, US seismologists said, with authorities reporting minor injuries to three people, according to a preliminary report ( archived link ).

The Geophysical Institute of Peru (IGP) put the magnitude at 7.2 and said the quake occurred at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).

In Peru, at least 22 homes, six schools and 12 medical centres have been impacted by the quake, the preliminary report found, as officials continue making damage assessments.

The tremor is the latest in a string of powerful quakes to strike South America, following deadly quakes in Venezuela on June 24 and Colombia on August 10 (archived here and here ).

Similar claims circulated across Weibo and Douyin and also spread in multiple languages such as Spanish and Japanese .

But the clip shows a quake in Colombia and not Peru.

A reverse image search on Google found an Instagram post that shared a similar photo showing the damaged blue building on August 13 ( archived link ). Its caption says Pereira.

A 7.4-magnitude tremor struck Colombia on August 10, the most powerful to hit the country in nearly half a century ( archived link ).

The quake killed nearly 300 people and destroyed more than 27,000 homes, with Pereira one of the cities affected the most ( archived link )

Google Maps street imagery of Carrera 7a in Pereira, Risaralda department, Colombia from March 2024 matches the scene in the false post ( archived link ).

Diaro del Otun, a media organisation based in Pereira, also published several photos of the same area on its Facebook account ( archived link ).

"Calle 32 at the junction of Carrera 6 and 9, Pereira...This is the state of these areas in central Pereira following the damage caused by the earthquake," the post's caption says.

AFP has debunked false claims related to recent quakes in South America.

The video shows the upper half of a blue building collapsing and debris falling as a man yells, "grandma, grandma...no...no" in Spanish.

A strong 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck southern Peru on August 20, US seismologists said, with authorities reporting minor injuries to three people, according to a preliminary report ( archived link ).
The Geophysical Institute of Peru (IGP) put the magnitude at 7.2 and said the quake occurred at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).
In Peru, at least 22 homes, six schools and 12 medical centres have been impacted by the quake, the preliminary report found, as officials continue making damage assessments.
The tremor is the latest in a string of powerful quakes to strike South America, following deadly quakes in Venezuela on June 24 and Colombia on August 10 (archived here and here ).
Similar claims circulated across Weibo and Douyin and also spread in multiple languages such as Spanish and Japanese .
But the clip shows a quake in Colombia and not Peru.
A reverse image search on Google found an Instagram post that shared a similar photo showing the damaged blue building on August 13 ( archived link ). Its caption says Pereira.
A 7.4-magnitude tremor struck Colombia on August 10, the most powerful to hit the country in nearly half a century ( archived link ).
The quake killed nearly 300 people and destroyed more than 27,000 homes, with Pereira one of the cities affected the most ( archived link )
Google Maps street imagery of Carrera 7a in Pereira, Risaralda department, Colombia from March 2024 matches the scene in the false post ( archived link ).
Diaro del Otun, a media organisation based in Pereira, also published several photos of the same area on its Facebook account ( archived link ).
"Calle 32 at the junction of Carrera 6 and 9, Pereira...This is the state of these areas in central Pereira following the damage caused by the earthquake," the post's caption says.
AFP has debunked false claims related to recent quakes in South America.

articles.title: 'They had gone towards Sargodha': Ex-Navy officer backs former CDS Anil Chauhan on Kirana Hills remarks
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Former director of naval operations and intelligence commodore Ranjit Rai (Retd.) on Tuesday said former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) Gener.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former director of naval operations and intelligence commodore Ranjit Rai (Retd.) on Tuesday said former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan's remarks on Pakistan's Kirana Hills indicated that Operation Sindoor was a "total success", particularly highlighting India's use of loitering munitions during the 87-hour military operation.Speaking to news agency ANI, Rai was reacting to Chauhan's remarks that an Indian loitering munition deployed to search for radars in and around Sargodha in Pakistan "must have" hit an area in the Kirana Hills after failing to locate its intended target."He made it absolutely clear that it was a total success (Operation Sindoor)," Rai told ANI. He said Chauhan had made it clear that during the 87-hour operation, loitering munitions were deployed and operated around Sargodha.Rai also pointed to the significance of Kirana Hills, located around 10 kilometres north of Sargodha."He disclosed that during the operation, loitering munitions, which are drones, were used. They were loitering 10 miles from Sargodha; they had gone towards Sargodha, but 10 miles from Sargodha is the Khirana Hills. Pakistan has carried out some critical nuclear tests at the Khirana Hills. Underground in Kirana, they have got some nuclear facility. I mean, this is a revolution, telling the world about Operation Sindoor," he said.Chauhan, speaking at the Vivekananda Centre in New Delhi on Tuesday, said India had sent loitering munitions towards Sargodha to search for radars in and around the area. He explained that the weapons had a flight time of around two hours and, if they failed to locate a target during that period, would eventually come down and hit an area."I think I'll clarify this...at occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit or not, which is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering munitions at Sargodha and Kirana Hills is about 10 kilometres north of Sargodha. So the loitering ammunition is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a lifetime, which means it will loiter for about two hours and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere," Chauhan said."It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked, because Pakistani media also showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills," he added.What Chauhan said about Kirana HillsChauhan's remarks clarified that Kirana Hills was not deliberately selected as a target during Operation Sindoor. Rather, according to his account, a loitering munition searching for radars around Sargodha may have struck one of the hills after failing to find its intended target.The comments also put his remarks in the context of an earlier statement by Air Marshal AK Bharti, who was director general of air operations during Operation Sindoor.On May 12, 2025, Bharti had rejected speculation that Indian forces had deliberately targeted Kirana Hills."Thank you for telling us that Kirana Hills houses some nuclear installations. We did not know about it. We have not hit Kirana Hills. I did not brief in my briefing yesterday," Bharti had said.Chauhan similarly referred to the earlier statement and explained that the possible impact on Kirana Hills was linked to the operation of loitering munitions sent towards Sargodha.Operation Sindoor was launched by India following the Pahalgam terror attack in which 26 people were killed.The Indian Armed Forces targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK). As Pakistan sought to escalate the conflict, India also struck Pakistani airbases before Pakistan sought a ceasefire.Chauhan also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had given the military "complete freedom of action" before Operation Sindoor and told the armed forces to decide the timing of the operation while ensuring there was no scope for failure.The ex-CDS had said the Prime Minister told the military to act at its own time, ensure there was no reason for failure, maintain evidence of the actions taken and exercise "complete freedom of action."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Man seen in Philadelphia wearing creepy, Chucky-style mask is arrested in Las Vegas, authorities say
articles.summary: An arrest warrant was issued in Philadelphia after a masked man chased a jogger there and said, “Are you ready to die?” Authorities say he wanted to boost his social media views.
articles.body: A man alleged to have been seen in Philadelphia wearing a creepy, Chucky-style mask and harassing people there last week was arrested in Las Vegas, authorities in the desert city said Tuesday. Zymire Hughes was arrested by members of the U.S. Marshals Service Violent Offender Task Force, the service said in a statement. Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said last week that the warrant is based on allegations of felony and misdemeanor assault after a masked man chased a jogger, asked, “Do you want to die?” and caused her to suffer injuries as she fled early last Wednesday in Center City. He said that more charges were possible and that they would be outlined after the suspect was arrested. Booking information from the Clark County Detention Center in Nevada shows Hughes in custody with no bail, with a hearing before a judge scheduled for Thursday morning. It’s not clear whether he has legal counsel. Public defender’s offices in Clark County, Nevada, and Philadelphia did not immediately respond to requests for comment after regular business hours late Tuesday. Police allege Hughes approached more than a dozen people in Center City before he fled after his interaction with the jogger. Police said he fled again after regional transit police in a train station contacted him and told him to remove his mask. Authorities followed a trail via security cameras in the city that led to an apartment building where, they say, Hughes lives. Three people identified the masked suspect as Hughes, police said at a news conference last week. The mask resembles the killer doll from the “Child’s Play” horror movie franchise. Police believe the masked man may have behaved in this manner before, and they asked any other possible victims to come forward. A few days after the Center City incidents, Philadelphia Police Capt. Jason Smith said, police were tipped off that the suspect was alleged to have packed his bags and left the apartment. Krasner said Hughes is on probation for an unspecified crime in nearby Montgomery County. Smith said the suspect has two TikTok accounts and one Instagram account. He wore the mask to draw people to his online presence, Krasner said. “We’re not having it in this city,” Krasner said of the antics. “We are not tolerating it.”

articles.title: Klay Thompson reveals real reason for $9.8 million sacrifice to join Miami Heat
articles.summary: New Miami Heat swingman Klay Thompson explained why he was willing to give up almost $10 million to ensure he could switch teams this offseason. Thompson spe...
articles.body:
New Miami Heat swingman Klay Thompson explained why he was willing to give up almost $10 million to ensure he could switch teams this offseason.

Thompson spent most of the offseason as a member of the Dallas Mavericks and was owed $17.4 million over the 2026-27 season, the final one under contract for Thompson.

After no favorable trades emerged for Klay, the Mavericks and the 36-year-old negotiated a contract buyout, one where Thompson gave up $9.8 million to become a free agent and sign with the Heat.

Klay Thompson values winning over anything

Thompson spoke to the media at his introduction as a new member of the Miami Heat, revealing that the opportunity to compete for a title was more important than maximising his NBA earnings.

"Just the opportunity to play high-level basketball and a chance to make a deep postseason run. Those things were so attractive to me. Obviously you want to maximize your earnings as an athlete, but I've tasted winning before, and there's nothing like it"

The Mavericks are an intriguing young team led by Cooper Flagg , but they have a lot more steps to become contenders again. Thompson signed with them in 2024 because they were fresh off a Finals run with Luka Doncic leading the franchise.

That reality changed quickly, and now Klay is hoping to play postseason basketball on a team with title hopes again after missing the playoffs for the last two seasons.

Thompson averaged 11.7 points on 38.3% from three with the Mavericks last season.

The days when he was an All-Defense caliber two-way player are long gone, but Klay is still one of the best shooters in the NBA.

The Heat are led by two frontcourt players in Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo , so Klay plays an important role as an elite shooter who is bound to get open opportunities playing off the two big men.

Thompson will have to compete with Tim Hardaway Jr. and Pelle Larsson for the starting shooting guard spot on the Heat, with Davion Mitchell and Andrew Wiggins likely locked into the starting five.

Hardaway Jr. has proven he can be a bench scoring specialist, so he's likely not going to start. Larsson has defensive upside and scoring ability but likely won't match Klay's offensive consistency and off-ball play.

His role will be interesting to see shape up over the season, as the Heat hope to be contenders.

articles.title: Brandon Miller gets realistic about the Charlotte Hornets ahead of the 2026-27 season
articles.summary: Brandon Miller has a steady perspective regarding the Hornets.
articles.body:
Brandon Miller gets realistic about the Charlotte Hornets ahead of the 2026-27 season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Trading away LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges is a big shift for the Charlotte Hornets ahead of the 2026-27 season. They are intent on building around Brandon Miller and Kon Knueppel moving forward, but it seems that will take a while before it can fully get going.

They have missed the postseason for the past decade, which was when Kemba Walker was still leading the charge for the Hornets . Something had to change with the Hornets, and it seems that they are doing so for the 2026-27 season. It won't be the prettiest, but they are prepared to fight with this current roster.

Brandon Miller sets realistic expectations for the Hornets

Now that the Hornets have ushered in a new era, there is a fair bit of excitement around the organization. Everyone knows that this is a new era for the team, so they are ready to prove themselves. However, it seems that Miller is not getting ahead of himself.

Miller knows that the new-look Hornets will need time to adjust, especially with the lack of game-changing talent. Both Knueppel and Miller have the potential to do so, but they will still need reps as the star players. They are still young, so they need to prove themselves first.

MORE: The Hornets' front office addresses the reason why they traded both LaMelo Ball and Miles Bridges

At the same time, the front office is only getting started, so there will most likely be moves with the roster. Knueppel and Miller are stamped as the building blocks, but the rest of the team will need to be worked on. There are plenty of high-potential players in Charlotte, but it should mean that they are still in the development process.

"Do I know if we are going to be good or great? I know we are going to be a hard-working team. It's not about who makes the most shots. It's about who can play consistently at 110% every night. I think that's one thing we are going to take pride in," Miller said to The Charlotte Observer about the future .

As long as the Hornets are intent on building around Knueppel and Miller, they have a bright future. However, that was also said about Ball and Bridges, so the Hornets have to prove that they can be smart in the market, so they can keep building around this project they're working on.

articles.title: White Sox outlast Rangers in South Side slugfest, 11-7
articles.summary: Tristan Peters mashed his fourth homer in as many games as Chicago rebounded to defeat Texas
articles.body:
Both teams came out swinging tonight, combining for 25 hits and 18 runs, but the White Sox (69-63) beat up on Jacob deGrom and outlasted the Rangers (66-67), 11-7. I'd be lying if I said I wasn't nervous getting through this one, but this was a huge win for the South Siders coming off a blowout loss, and at the very least they will still hold a 2 1/2-game lead over the Cleveland Guardians .

The South Side offense snapped back to life Tuesday and absolutely dominated deGrom, plating six in the bottom of the first after batting around, sending Anthony Kay into the second with plenty of run support. It's clear that deGrom wasn't on his A game, but the Good Guys were much more selective and patient at the plate, striking out just twice against the righthander while walking five times. It marked the second time in just a few weeks that the veteran walked five batters in an outing.

Things got out of control fairly quickly for the former Cy Young Award winner. Sam Antonacci led off the game with a double, and deGrom subsequently walked Munetaka Murakami to put two aboard for the hot-hitting Miguel Vargas . The Rangers didn't record an out until Chase Meidroth popped out to first baseman Jake Burger in foul territory with the bases loaded, but the White Sox had already pushed across two runs. Vargas hit a single to left, while a throwing error by Wyatt Langford allowed Antonacci to score and moved Mune to third. Braden Montgomery followed with a line-drive base hit to left that brought home Murakami and made it 2-0.

Speaking of staying hot, Tristan Peters came through in the clutch yet again, mashing a broken-bat double that put two more runs on the scoreboard and stretched the lead to 4-0. With Peters and Colson Montgomery on second and third, Brenton Doyle kept the hit train rolling, singling up the middle to drive in both runners and make it 6-0.

deGrom walked his final two batters to put two aboard in the bottom of the fourth. Although he induced a ground ball, the Rangers couldn't complete the double play, prompting Skip Schumaker to turn to the bullpen to stop the bleeding. Immediately after Cole Winn replaced him, Colson and Meidroth mashed back-to-back RBI singles to tack on two more insurance runs, both of which were charged to deGrom. The veteran righthander ended his 3 2/3-inning outing with eight runs allowed on six hits, raising his ERA to 4.21.

Lefthander Anthony Kay looked sharp for most of his outing, allowing only one run through the first four frames: a solo homer by Jake Burger to center. But a switch flipped in the top of the fifth, and Kay surrendered three more runs before Jordan Hicks replaced him with two outs. It was a wild sequence after four innings of solid work: Cody Freeman singled, a wild pitch moved him to second, Danny Jansen blasted a two-run homer, and Kay hit Justin Foscue with a pitch. It was the 25th batter Kay has hit this season, the most among major league pitchers.

Kay recorded two big outs by striking out Corey Seager and Brandon Nimmo , though he walked Langford between the two strikeouts, moving Foscue into scoring position. Ezequiel Duran then ripped an RBI single to left, and that was the last straw for Will Venable , who turned to Hicks to shut Texas down. Kay ultimately allowed four runs on six hits — including two home runs — with two walks and four strikeouts, raising his ERA slightly to 4.09. The move to Hicks worked perfectly, as he struck out Burger to end the inning and prevent any additional runs from being charged to Kay.

The good news for the White Sox was that the offense kept rolling, getting two of those three runs back in the bottom half of the inning. Drew Romo walked to lead off the frame, and Antonacci smashed a triple into the right-field corner as the next batter, scoring Romo all the way from first. Although he still should not be part of the White Sox's future catching plans, Romo has stepped it up offensively over his last seven games, posting a much more respectable .222/.364/.389 slash line with a .753 OPS. Vargas mashed his second hit of the night to drive in Antonacci for the South Siders' 10th run, restoring their six-run lead at 10-4.

In the blink of an eye, the Rangers offense made things uncomfortable again. After scoring three runs in consecutive innings, Texas had trimmed the lead to 10-7 and put the game within striking distance. Hicks fell apart in the sixth, allowing a pinch-hit single to Joc Pederson before Jansen doubled him home. Justin Foscue then blasted a two-run homer to turn the game into a full-fledged slugfest.

In the bottom of the sixth, the Good Guys answered back. They didn't get all three runs back, but Peters provided one with a solo bomb — his fourth home run in as many games. Peters has been on a tear lately, slugging .909 over his last seven games with a double and four homers, good for a 1.309 OPS. The homer was Peters' third hit of the night, leaving him a triple shy of the cycle.

Peters came up once more in the bottom of the eighth with Meidroth on first after his third hit of the night, but former White Sox pitcher Tyler Alexander didn't want to give him anything to hit. Alexander issued him a four-pitch walk, allowing Peters to reach base for the fifth time in the game.

Both bullpens surrendered three runs after the starters departed, but lefthanders Bryan Hudson and Hagen Smith were able to pick up Hicks over the next three innings. Hudson came in to put out the fire in the sixth, then worked a 1-2-3 seventh to halt the momentum Texas had built. Smith was set to handle the final two innings, and the lefty was excellent in the eighth despite allowing a double to Justin Foscue for his second hit of the night. The Rangers couldn't build on it, and Smith struck out Seager to end the inning. Foscue's double was just the second hit Smith had allowed since being called up to the big leagues, showing how nasty he can be when he commands his pitches.

Unfortunately, Smith couldn't maintain that command and made things a little too interesting in the top of the ninth. He walked three batters to load the bases with two outs, putting the Rangers one swing away from tying the game at 11-11 — and one swing away from potentially giving me a heart attack. Venable wasn't taking any chances with Smith's inconsistency, so he called on Grant Taylor to shut things down and record the final out. Taylor did just that. With two pitches, the righty secured his eighth save of the season and a much-needed win for the South Siders.

As of publication, both the Twins and Guardians are losing, so it would be lovely for the White Sox to gain a full game on both teams. The Sox need to keep their heads down, take it one at-bat at a time and play their game. When they play loose like they did tonight, they can do plenty of damage at the plate. paragraphs: Both teams came out swinging tonight, combining for 25 hits and 18 runs, but the White Sox (69-63) beat up on Jacob deGrom and outlasted the Rangers (66-67), 11-7. The South Side offense snapped back to life Tuesday and absolutely dominated deGrom, plating six in the bottom of the first after batting around, sending Anthony Kay into the second with plenty of run support. It marked the second time in just a few weeks that the veteran walked five batters in an outing.

Vargas hit a single to left, while a throwing error by Wyatt Langford allowed Antonacci to score and moved Mune to third. Braden Montgomery followed with a line-drive base hit to left that brought home Murakami and made it 2-0.

deGrom walked his final two batters to put two aboard in the bottom of the fourth. Although he induced a ground ball, the Rangers couldn't complete the double play, prompting Skip Schumaker to turn to the bullpen to stop the bleeding. Immediately after Cole Winn replaced him, Colson and Meidroth mashed back-to-back RBI singles to tack on two more insurance runs, both of which were charged to deGrom. The veteran righthander ended his 3 2/3-inning outing with eight runs allowed on six hits, raising his ERA to 4.21.

Lefthander Anthony Kay looked sharp for most of his outing, allowing only one run through the first four frames: a solo homer by Jake Burger to center. But a switch flipped in the top of the fifth, and Kay surrendered three more runs before Jordan Hicks replaced him with two outs. It was a wild sequence after four innings of solid work: Cody Freeman singled, a wild pitch moved him to second, Danny Jansen blasted a two-run homer, and Kay hit Justin Foscue with a pitch. It was the 25th batter Kay has hit this season, the most among major league pitchers.

Ezequiel Duran then ripped an RBI single to left, and that was the last straw for Will Venable , who turned to Hicks to shut Texas down. The move to Hicks worked perfectly, as he struck out Burger to end the inning and prevent any additional runs from being charged to Kay.

Drew Romo walked to lead off the frame, and Antonacci smashed a triple into the right-field corner as the next batter, scoring Romo all the way from first. Vargas mashed his second hit of the night to drive in Antonacci for the South Siders' 10th run, restoring their six-run lead at 10-4.

In the blink of an eye, the Rangers offense made things uncomfortable again. After scoring three runs in consecutive innings, Texas had trimmed the lead to 10-7 and put the game within striking distance. Hicks fell apart in the sixth, allowing a pinch-hit single to Joc Pederson before Jansen doubled him home. Justin Foscue then blasted a two-run homer to turn the game into a full-fledged slugfest.

In the bottom of the sixth, the Good Guys answered back. They didn't get all three runs back, but Peters provided one with a solo bomb — his fourth home run in as many games. Unfortunately, Smith couldn't maintain that command and made things a little too interesting in the top of the ninth. He walked three batters to load the bases with two outs, putting the Rangers one swing away from tying the game at 11-11 — and one swing away from potentially giving me a heart attack. Venable wasn't taking any chances with Smith's inconsistency, so he called on Grant Taylor to shut things down and record the final out. Taylor did just that. articles.title: Chicago Cubs score 30 unanswered runs over 3 straight games, setting franchise record
articles.summary: The Chicago Cubs set a franchise record on Tuesday by scoring their 30th unanswered run over three games, breaking the previous record of 29 over a three-gam...
articles.body:
PHOENIX (AP) — The Chicago Cubs set a franchise record on Tuesday by scoring their 30th unanswered run over three games, breaking the previous record of 29 over a three-game stretch in 1969.

The Cubs started the streak on Sunday, falling behind 2-0 in the early innings against the Seattle Mariners before rallying for a 19-2 win.

Chicago then blanked the Arizona Diamondbacks 7-0 on Monday and jumped to a 4-0 lead in Tuesday's game against the D-backs.

The previous record of 29 happened in 1876 and more recently from May 11-13 in 1969, according to Elias Sports Bureau. During that stretch, the Cubs shut out the San Francisco Giants 8-0 before beating the San Diego Padres 2-0 and 19-0 in consecutive games.

articles.title: Frank Reich Shares Brutal Honesty With Jets TE Kenyon Sadiq
articles.summary: New York Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich shared some brutal honesty with first round tight end Kenyon Sadiq. The post Frank Reich Shares Brutal Honest...
articles.body:
When the New York Jets invested the No. 16 overall pick in the first round on tight end Kenyon Sadiq, he was expected to play a major role on the offense.

What about now, after he has missed so much time due to injury this offseason? Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich shared some brutal honesty at the podium.

"Yeah, there's no doubt we will have to scale it back. We just gotta work him in slowly. We can't rush it, as much as we would like to. The good thing is he's very smart, and we've said it all before, but he will be as ready as you can go, but there's nothing like practice. I know he has stayed locked in, but we gotta get back out on the practice field and just slowly work him back into the mix," Reich explained.

This wasn't a surprising answer from Reich, but it confirmed what many have speculated.

Sadiq had high expectations as the No. 16 overall pick in the first round of April's draft. He was the highest drafted tight end by the Jets since Dustin Keller was the No. 30 overall pick in the first round of the 2008 NFL draft.

However, he has missed some critical time this offseason.

He had sports hernia surgery in May that forced him to miss the final week of OTAs and all of mandatory minicamp.

Sadiq looked like gangbusters through the first several days of training camp, but he suffered "a little bit of a setback" on August 4. "He missed the final 12 practices of training camp, which concluded Tuesday," ESPN's Rich Cimini wrote.

That will also include the entire preseason. These are critical reps for any player, let alone a rookie.

Cimini said Sadiq was used like a "chess piece," with the coaches having him serve in "a variety of roles" in the first three practices of camp when he was healthy.

The more you ask someone to do, the more of the playbook they have to master. Sadiq was lining up in-line, at H-back, in the backfield, and split out as a wide receiver during my observations of training camp. The lack of physical reps will limit the type of impact he can have, at least early on in the season.

It stinks to have an impact player on the shelf, but if there's any consolation for the Jets, it's their depth.

ESPN's Rich Cimini told NFL Insider Ari Meirov that the Jets believe that "they have one of the deepest tight end rooms in the league."

Beyond Sadiq, that group includes Mason Taylor , Jeremy Ruckert , and Jelani Woods .

Taylor has been popping in camp in Sadiq's absence. With all of his missed time, Taylor has taken full advantage. On top of those additional reps in practice, Taylor got extra work in with starting quarterback Geno Smith during the break.

That chemistry is translating to the field.

During the final training camp practice of the summer, Taylor "mossed" star safety Minkah Fitzpatrick on a big play.

The Jets posted the highlight clip on X with the caption, "Catch-of-camp nominee."

If this is any indication of what's to come, it seems like the Jets will be just fine without Sadiq while he gets right.
